submission.natural_language_explanation: This head binds bibliographic metadata to its publication venue: in reference-style strings it writes strongly at the numeric field tokens that follow a journal, proceedings or law-reporter title (e.g. 'Annals of Probability, 2018, 46 (3)', 'Scientific Reports | (2022) 12:21071', '199 F.3d 244, 249-50 (4th Cir. 1999)'), and its attention goes back to that venue token (' Probability', ' Reports', the 'd' of 'F.3d'), not to the preceding token. The numbers' values are irrelevant and the same numbers in prose, in author-year citations such as '(Smith, 1999)', or before the venue do not fire; the same write recurs at a later use of a declared identifier in code (e.g. 'tcs' after 'TaskCompletionSource', attending 'Source').

rival_explanations: A generic number/date detector: the head fires on any year- or volume-like number wherever it appears, and references merely dominate the scan because that is where such tokens cluster (it predicts strong activation for years/volumes in ordinary prose, e.g. 'In 2018, 46 papers appeared').

A duplicate/second-mention head: the real trigger is a repeated token or repeated record format (identifier re-use after its declaration, numeric fields repeating a reference template seen earlier), and the journal-title attention is incidental (it predicts strong activation for repeated names or repeated tokens outside references, and for citation numbers even when no venue name is present).
